newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa wants to up stake in Cepsa, revise BCH deal.
newsitem.headline: Endesa wants to up stake in Cepsa, revise BCH deal.

text.p: Spanish electricity company Endesa wants to raise its stake in energy group Cepsa, Chairman Rodolfo Martin Villa said on Friday.
Speaking to journalists at a lunch, he added that the group also wants to revise the deal they did some years ago with Banco Central Hispano BCH.
"We want to review the deal with BCH and change the fields that the collaboration encompasses without a rupture," he said.
At present Endesa has a eight percent stake in Cepsa.
"Endesa wants to increase its stake in Cepsa, and there is five percent available," Martin Villa said.
Endesa and BCH made a deal several years ago when the bank bought a one percent stake in the electrical company with the option to buy another two percent.
But the agreement was put in danger when Endesa and BCH put in bids for the privatisation of Retevision in separate groups.
The Endesa chairman added that if it were impossible to increase its stake in Cepsa, the electricity company would consider selling its holding in Cepsa.
"We want to be a core shareholder (in Cepsa)," he said.
Regarding the BCH deal, Martin Villa added that "from a certain point of view this deal does not make sense anymore".
As regards Retevision Martin Villa said an agreement with BCH was unlikely.
"We have to behave with loyalty to our technological partner (Stet )", he said.
